text:
Erik Karlsson turned 36 this year and is still playing 23:27 a night, still putting up points (18 in 18 games, half on the power play) and still capable of a 97 mph one-timer. The trouble is the five-on-five picture around him: Pittsburgh gets 47% of the expected goals with him on, and the team is better by that measure when he sits. On a struggling Penguins team, his name is in the same trade columns as Evgeni Malkin's.

The skill is not the question. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile of defensemen for primary shot assists last season and stopping entries at his blue line more often than typical. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 23rd among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, against 97th-percentile competition.

His scoring rate is above our talent range (2.56 points per 60 against 1.85 to 2.49), so expect a little cooling. Our projection still lands him around 75 points, which is a lot of value for whoever has him in March.
headline: Karlsson still drives the bus, uphill
